News.title: At least seven injured after Benidorm hotel roof COLLAPSES on holidaymakers as emergency services race to scene
News.content:
HOLS HORROR At least seven injured after Benidorm hotel roof COLLAPSES on holidaymakers as emergency services race to scene

AT least seven people have been injured when the ceiling of a Benidorm hotel collapsed over them on Easter Sunday.

Sections of plasterboard and air conditioning ducts crashed onto around 60 guests dining at Poseidón Palace.





Among the victims were an eight-year-old boy and 78-year-old man who were later discharged after receiving treatment.

Five other people aged between 33 and 80 were hospitalised, with one of them now under observation at Hospital de la Marina Baixa.

For now, the reason for the collapse is still unclear – but this is not the first such incident to have plagued the Benidorm hotel scene.

Around 900,000 British tourists flock to Benidorm every year, making it a primary destination for UK holidaymakers in Spain.

News.title: Inside US airman’s Iran rescue worthy of Hollywood thriller from CIA deception plan to ‘ring of steel’ & ‘walls of fire’
News.content:
AN INJURED US airman, armed only with a handgun and stranded deep inside enemy territory, had a slim survival rate as Iranian militants closed in.

But the mission – reckoned by experts to be the most challenging in Special Forces history – involved hundreds of elite troops, dozens of aircraft and a CIA deception campaign.





Commandos from the legendary Navy Seal Team which killed Osama Bin Laden landed deep in a remote mountainous region to rescue the seriously injured airman.

Both the pilot and the weapons systems officer (WSO), who sits behind and is also known as the backseater, had been forced to eject when their F-15E Strike Eagle was hit by Iranian air defences on Friday.

The pilot was rescued within a few hours but the WSO, a highly experienced aviator with the rank of Colonel, could not be located.

It sparked a desperate life-or-death race between American and Iranian forces to reach him first.

Mullahs placed a £50,000 bounty on his head leading to packs of semi-nomadic tribesmen – who survive on a weekly wage of £35 – joining the hunt armed with AK47s.

The incredible details of how the pilot survived and the daring mission to rescue him emerged after Donald Trump announced the good news that he had been found safe and well just after 5am UK time.

He had managed to eject and parachuted safely without Iranian forces observing his landing spot.

Nursing a serious leg injury and armed only with a handgun, he unclipped his harness and immediately put his Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape training into practice



The airman began climbing up the nearest peak to evade locals, at one stage scaling a 7,000ft mountain ridge before hiding in a crevice as he waited for help to arrive.

All flight crew are equipped with a beacon to transmit their location to central command as well as a secure communication device.

But it appears that the CIA were instrumental in pinpointing his location.

As Special Forces units were fine-tuning the details of their Combat Search and Rescue mission ready for when he was found, CIA spooks launched a deception campaign.

Utilising local contacts and other methods, they spread rumours that the airman had been rescued and was being evacuated out of Iran in a ground convoy.



They also contacted local farmers and shepherds who are not hugely loyal to the regime in the hope they might assist, a tactic known as “unconventional assisted recovery.”

Dozens of aircraft including Black Hawk and HH-60G Pave Hawk helicopters had been in the skies from the moment the F-15 went down looking for the crew.

A C-130 Hercules transporter plane and a HC-130J Combat King II – America’s only dedicated personnel recovery plane – were also scrambled.

On board were a variety of Special Forces units, including America’s primary Search and Rescue unit, the Parerescuemen.

Dubbed the “tip of the spear” for difficult rescues, the Pararescue Unit are among the most highly trained Special Forces in the World.



Part of the 52nd Expeditionary Rescue Squadron, they parachute into combat zones with 470sq ft parachutes, twice the size of a regular chute, so they can carry huge amounts of equipment including an 80-pound parachute pack containing emergency medical kit such as packs of blood.

They often work alongside other Special Forces units which on this mission included Navy Seal Team 6 who took out Al Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden in a night time raid in Pakistan in 2011.

After more than 24 hours of intense work, the CIA eventually located the airman on Saturday.

They passed his co-ordinates to the Pentagon and the incredible rescue mission worthy of a Hollywood thriller swung into action.



Israel assisted by launching a huge blitz of more than 120 targets, effectively laying down a vast carpet of covering fire.

American troops did the same, dropping bombs and opening fire on Iranian military convoys to clear the way for “one of the most challenging and complex missions in the history of US special operations”, according to one American official.

Under the cover of darkness late on Saturday – and with huge numbers of Iranian troops closing in – the Navy Seals landed close to the airman on an HH-60W Jolly Green II chopper.

They carried out a swift identity check, a process that likely included at least one question based on information in his Isolated Personnel Report (ISOPREP) that only he would know the answer to.

The document, held by the intelligence section of his unit, contains photographs, fingerprints and personal info and was passed to those co-ordinating his rescue.



As the Seals were confirming his ID, MQ-9 Reaper drones were helping maintain a ring of steel by firing on Iranian military-aged males believed to be a threat if they came within two miles.

Iranian officials later said ten people had been killed in the province.

Once the airman’s ID was confirmed he was taken aboard the Jolly Green ‘copter and flown to Kuwait for medical treatment.



But in a final, heart stopping twist, two MC-130 military transport planes taking part in the op got stuck in sand at a temporary air base the USAF had built in a remote area.

Three other planes had to be scrambled to rescue the crews and Special Forces soldiers then destroyed the stranded aircraft to prevent sensitive info falling into Iranian hands.

Pictures published later suggested that at least two MH-6M Little Birds, helicopters used in special operations, were also destroyed.

Trump has hailed the stunning rescue as an “Easter miracle”.

The president revealed he had been seriously wounded but “will be just fine”.



He later texted reporters: “The rescue was an ‘Easter miracle. The enemy was large and violent. The rescuers were brilliant, strong, decisive and as cool as anyone can be.'”

It was feared the WSO may have died in the crash after it was announced that the pilot had been rescued.

An American official hailed the CIA’s deception campaign, saying: “While the Iranians were confused and uncertain of what was happening, the Agency used its unique, exquisite capabilities to search for – and find – the American.

“This was the ultimate ‘needle in a haystack,’ but in this case it was a brave American soul inside a mountain crevice, invisible but for CIA’s capabilities.”

The mission was celebrated in America and Israel – led by Mr Trump, who described it as “one of the most daring Search and Rescue Operations in U.S. History.”



He said: “This brave Warrior was behind enemy lines in the treacherous mountains of Iran, being hunted down by our enemies, who were getting closer and closer by the hour.

“The fact that we were able to pull off both of these operations, without a SINGLE American killed, or even wounded, just proves once again, that we have achieved overwhelming Air Dominance and Superiority over the Iranian skies.”

Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said: “I congratulate Donald Trump on the rescue of a brave American pilot by America’s courageous warriors.

“All Israelis rejoice in this remarkable operation.”

America’s Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz, a former Army Green Beret, said: “America breathes a sigh of relief. More amazing work by my special operations brothers.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Meanwhile, the Pope appealed for peace in his Easter blessing at the Vatican.

Pope Leo XIV urged “those who have the power to unleash wars” to “choose peace” instead and criticised global indifference to “the deaths of thousands of people”.

News.title: Keir Starmer is taking us back to 1970s like crew of Artemis II – but unlike brave astronauts, his mission is rudderless
News.content:
It’s not the excitement of the space race he has rekindled, though, but a return to stubborn inflation, rising unemployment and faltering growth

DAVID WOODING Keir Starmer is taking us back to 1970s like crew of Artemis II – but unlike brave astronauts, his mission is rudderless

FOUR brave astronauts will be the first humans to visit the moon in 50 years today – but back on Earth it’s Keir Starmer who faces the final ­frontier.

His five-year mission to explore new policies and find life in the economy could be cut short by a bloodbath in next month’s local elections.





Like the crew of Artemis II, the PM has taken us back to the 1970s.

It’s not the excitement of the space race he has rekindled, though, but a return to stubborn inflation, rising unemployment and faltering growth.

Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell, the sixth man to walk on the moon, once declared: “From out there on the moon, international politics looks so petty. You want to grab a politician by the scruff of the neck, drag him a quarter of a ­million miles out and say, ‘Look at that, you son of a bitch’.”

Right now, the Cabinet could do with a rocket under them.



So for fun, here’s a look at what would happen if Sir Keir decided to cautiously go where no man has gone before.

The spaceship Continuity II is on the launchpad with ­Commander Starmer on board, with crew Rachel Reeves, Ed Miliband and David Lammy.

‘Ed, you’re in charge’

The countdown begins: “Ten . . . nine . . . eight . . . seven . . .”

Starmer: “Can we stop for a moment for a rethink? Let’s get a Cabinet sub-committee to review our direction first.”



Reeves: “Not another relaunch, Keir? You’ve had three already and it hasn’t made an ounce of difference.”

Starmer: “Look, while the idea of boldly going where no one has gone before is admirable, it’s essential first to ­establish a clear framework for going, consult extensively with onboard stakeholders and ensure the mission does not break international law.”

Miliband: “I’ll have to over-rule you, commander. Nothing should delay the count­down hitting Net Zero on time.”

Starmer: “Oh, OK, Ed. I ­forgot. You’re in charge.”

Ground control: “Four . . . three . . . two . . . one . . . We have lift off.”



Starmer: “Wow! Why didn’t you use those rocket boosters on the economy, Rachel?”

Before leaving Earth’s orbit, the loo packs up.

Mission ­control tells them: “You want to come back to the UK? Nothing works here these days.”

After a leak inquiry, Starmer fixes the problem.



He beams: “Luckily, I have the technical know-how. Did I ever tell you my father was a toolmaker?”

Soon, Lammy pipes up: “We seem to be going round in ­circles. We’re back where we started. Have you performed another U-turn?”

Starmer: “Don’t be ridiculous. Our spacecraft is making an orbital recalibration. Besides, in zero gravity every movement is technically forward.”

Miliband gets out his ­guitar and the crew enjoy a sing-song, with apologies to the late David Bowie.

The heating’s switched off and the lights are low, oh-oh



I can’t afford the fuel, my car won’t go, oh-oh,

But he gives us frozen rail fares for us to go nowhere at all.

Sir Keir tells us he has a big pla-a-an,

But it keeps on changing and I don’t understa-a-and,

Says he’s gonna fix it but it seems like deja-vu to me.



There’s a Starmer waiting in the sky.

Right now, the Cabinet could do with a rocket under them

We’d like to re-elect him but the taxes are too high.

There’s a Starmer waiting in the sky

The cost of living’s going up, there’s nothing we can buy.

He told me: Let the people pay, let the migrants stay, let all the people pay.



An alarm interrupts the music-making.

Starmer calls ground control: “Euston, we have a problem. Euston, do you read me?”

There is silence for several nerve-racking seconds before the radio crackles into life.

“Sorry about that,” says the voice. “Morgan McSweeney’s transmitter was stolen again. He’s lost all your messages. What’s the problem?”

Starmer: “Our fuel tank ­indicator shows we are running on empty.”



Miliband: “Oh, that’ll be because I banned the ground crew from filling up before we left. The mission can’t be ­reliant on fossil fuels. We are going to the moon and back on wind power.”

Despite being rudderless and having no sense of direction, Continuity II finally drifts to the moon and, gazing down at the surface, the crew spots a suspicious craft in the Sea of Tranquility. Is it alien migrants?

Starmer: “But there’s no air in space. It’s just a vacuum.”

Miliband: “A bit like decision-making in Downing Street.”

Starmer: “Look, we promised voters the moon back in 2024 and we have to deliver it.”

Reeves: “I hope the moon is going to pay its fair share to fund this mission.”



Despite being rudderless and having no sense of direction, Continuity II finally drifts to the moon and, gazing down at the surface, the crew spots a suspicious craft in the Sea of Tranquility. Is it alien migrants?

‘Little green men’

Starmer: “I will not allow this to break our determination to smash the lunar gangs.

“I’ve pledged millions more to the French in the hope of reaching a one-in, one-out deal with Mars.”

Lammy points to the Apollo 11 landing site and says: “Next time we land on the moon, we must consider removing all flags left by previous astronauts.



“They are reminders of ­inter-galactic imperialism. We wouldn’t want to offend those little green men, especially those in Zack Polanski’s party.”

As Continuity II disappears behind the far side of the moon, the crew lose radio contact with Earth for 41 minutes.

Ground control: “That’s the most sense we’ve heard from you since you took power. Can you hear me, Major Keir? Can you hear me, Major Keir? Can you . . . ”

Starmer:

Here am I floating in my tin can,



Far above the moon.

I don’t know what to do,

So let’s rejoin the EU.

MINISTERS plan to tackle obesity with tighter controls on less healthy “junk” food.

But rising prices mean this is all some people can afford, and a crackdown will increase retail costs.



There’s only one solution . . . junk this badly timed idea.

KEMI BADENOCH has had a cracking Easter.

The Tory leader is growing into her role and people are starting to notice.



In a series of recent interviews, she displayed an air of quiet confidence, resilience and deep conviction.

She has also sussed out how best to rough up Sir Keir Starmer in their weekly Commons joust at Prime Minister’s Questions.

Her hard work paid dividends yesterday when a poll showed her outperforming all the major party leaders – 33 points ahead of the PM.

Luke Tryl, of pollsters More In Common, says: “Whereas last summer we’d run whole focus groups where no one would know who Kemi was, she is often now brought up spontaneously, and even some of those who would never vote Tory say they admire her conviction and straightforwardness.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Of course, there’s a long way to go to restore the Conservative Party’s battered reputation.



But she has stepped up the pace and Easter is the season of hope.

News.title: Man, 18, charged after ramming car into packed pub after ‘row with bouncer’ – as one left injured
News.content:
AN 18-YEAR-old man has been charged after allegedly ramming his car into a packed pub following a row with a bouncer.

Cops were called to The Dolphin bar in Broadstairs, Kent, in the early hours of Saturday morning after a black Seat Ibiza ploughed into the boozer.





A man in his 30s, understood to be the bouncer at the pub, was hospitalised in the crash with injuries to his leg and arm.

Police have since confirmed that Frank Finn, 18, has been charged with attempted grievous bodily harm with intent and dangerous driving.

Finn has been remanded into custody and is set to appear at Folkestone Magistrates’ Court tomorrow.

In an exclusive video shared with The Sun, a driver can be seen repeatedly crashing the black Seat Ibiza into the busy boozer.



Terrified onlookers could be heard screaming and scrambling for safety as the mayhem unfolded.

Witnesses said the carnage erupted moments after a man, believed to be the driver, was thrown out by a doorman following a disturbance inside.

They claimed he had been causing trouble in the pub before being booted out.

In the footage, staff can be heard shouting: “don’t let anyone out”, as the vehicle lines up outside the entrance.



It appears to wait at the junction opposite the pub for around 10 seconds before suddenly accelerating and smashing into the building.

The person filming backs into the doorway to avoid being hit as the car ploughs forward.

The driver then reverses before seemingly accelerating and smashing into the wall a second time.

After the collision, a man opens the passenger door and the driver appears to try and punch the person trying to apprehend him.

People can be heard screaming as Mark Morrison’s hit Return of the Mack blares in the background.



The driver then pulls away from the wrecked entrance, with debris wedged in the front of the vehicle, before speeding off from the scene.

Parts of the Seat were left behind among rubble ripped from the damaged pub building and scattered across the road.

A Kent Police spokesperson said: “A suspect has been charged in connection with a collision in Broadstairs.



“Kent Police was called to Albion Street Road at 1.56am on Saturday 4 April 2026 following a report that a car had collided with a building.

“Officers attended along with other emergency services. A man in his 30s was taken by paramedics to a local hospital after leg and arm injuries were reported.

“Initial enquiries were completed and a man was arrested a short while later.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“On Sunday April 5, Frank Finn, of High Street, Broadstairs, was charged with attempted grievous bodily harm with intent and dangerous driving.

“Mr Finn, 18, was remanded in custody to appear before Folkestone Magistrates’ Court the following day.”

News.title: Litter louts face massive fines under tough new crackdown to clean up Britain’s rubbish-strewn streets
News.content:
LITTER louts face being fined in the thousands under plans to crackdown on filthy streets.

The current maximum penalty for dropping the likes of crisps and cigarette packets on the street is £500 – far less harsh than the five-year prison sentence a judge can hand down for fly-tipping.



But ministers want to more than double the figure to fight the plague of rubbish tainting British streets.



Environment Secretary Emma Reynolds is understood to want to emulate Japan, where streets are pristine because the population abides strictly by social norms to never discard of rubbish outside a bin.

A government source said: “This Government is determined to restore pride in our communities. People shouldn’t have to put up with seeing litter and mess they didn’t create.

“Our approach is simple: the polluter pays – whether that’s organised waste crime or littering.

“Those who cause the mess must take responsibility, and we will look at every option to make that happen.”



Town halls in England dealt with an eye-watering 1.26 million fly-tipping cases last year, up 9 per cent on 2024.

Meanwhile, the number of fines issued to criminals fell by 9 per cent to just 1,250, while the combined value of fines plummeted by 8 per cent to £673,000.

News.title: Influencer Douglas Bispo Silva dies aged 21 after being shot while leaving street party
News.content:
DEATH TRAGEDY Influencer Douglas Bispo Silva dies aged 21 after being shot while leaving street party

A POPULAR influencer has tragically died after being shot dead when he was leaving a street party.

Douglas Bispo Silva, 21, was confirmed dead by Coletivo LGBTI+ Flores do Sisal, an LGBTQ+ organization based in Bahia, Brazil.





He was a member of the group.

In a harrowing Instagram statement, Douglas was remembered for his “presence and smile”.

“Another young life interrupted by the violence that insists on crossing our territories, our bodies, and our stories,” the post read.

Local media spoke to police, who said Douglas was shot outside a party in Alto da Bandeira – a rural Brazilian village – in the early hours of March 29.



He was pronounced dead at the scene.

A 24-year-old man who was also shot at the party was rushed to hospital by first responders.

He survived and was released on April 1.

An investigation has been launched into Douglas’ death.



Three men have been arrested, g1 and CNN Brasil reported.

Police say one of the trio may have produced the weapon used to kill the content creator.

Douglas was known for sharing his lifestyle content and dancing videos.

He had garnered 40,000 followers on Instagram.

Douglas last posted to his account on March 22, posing for the camera in a local street.



Fans have flooded the comments on his final post with tributes to the social media star.

One person said: “My God, such sad news, my friend, may God comfort the whole family”.

Another person wrote: “My condolences to the family”.

“Rest in peace my love,” a third said.

News.title: Zoo’s escaped capybara feared to have left search zone after expert tracker brought in to discover her finds no trace
News.content:
A CAPYBARA which is on the run from a zoo is feared to have fled from the area.

An expert animal tracker brought in by The Sun could find no trace of missing Samba.





The giant rodent escaped nearly three weeks ago.

Search teams mapped out a three square mile zone on the River Itchen where she is thought to be hiding and lined possible escape routes with humane badger traps.

But John Rhyder, 61, who was recruited by The Sun to join the hunt, found no trace of the nine-month-old.

John, who has worked with telly wildlife presenter Ray Mears, said: “My theory is she has found a quiet area inaccessible to humans, and especially dogs, to lay low.



“Other semi-aquatic mammals would do the same and there are acres of meadow along the river that are quiet and free from pets.

“I would say she is hiding in a reed bed with plenty of access to grass, on a quiet stretch of river.”

John, who did find evidence of deer, swans, ducks, voles, rats and herons, went on: “If she was along any of the river paths we would have seen some sign of her. Some footprints, some scat, or vegetation eaten.”

There have been sightings seven miles from Marwell Zoo, near Winchester.

Capybara, from South America, are the world’s biggest rodents.



They can grow to more than 5ft and weigh 12st.

News.title: Are YOU a psychopath? Take our quiz to see if your personality matches after 1 in 5 show ‘elevated’ traits
News.content:
THINK of psychopaths and you picture people like deranged cult leader Charles Manson and serial killer Ted Bundy.

But research suggests a large number of them walk among us — and you could even be a psychopath yourself.





People with clinical levels of ­psychopathy make up just one per cent of the population.

But these traits exist on a ­spectrum and everyone lands somewhere, from very low to very high.

Research suggests that between ten and 20 per cent of ­people have elevated levels of these traits, but are not clinically psychopaths.

Award-winning researcher and Associate Professor of Psychology, Leanne ten Brinke has spent years studying dark personalities.



She says: “We find these people everywhere. People with dark traits might not be serial killers or rapists — they can be the neighbour who delights in harassing us for no reason; the colleague who sabotages us behind our back; the partner who cheats on us while also trying to control us.

“Such individuals can be manipulative, narcissistic, impulsive, anti-social, callous and even sadistic, but that’s not all. They’re also a bit psychopathic.”

In her new book, Poisonous People, Leanne reveals how we can spot psychopathic traits in others — and ourselves.

She says: “Do you have a ­vindictive streak? Do you find yourself telling self-serving lies relatively often?



“Do you dominate ­conversations or relationships more than you should? Are you a tad over-competitive?

“Having engaged in a behaviour once doesn’t amount to a personality trait, but if you can recall multiple incidents of these behaviours, it suggests a concerning pattern.”

To see if you have psychopathic tendencies, take our test below and put a tick next to any act you’ve committed at least once.

Leanne says: “There is no specific number of check marks on this page that should raise alarm bells, but someone who has engaged in many of these behaviours likely harbours more elevated psychopathic traits than someone who has only ticked one or two.



“The distribution of your check marks across the test can also be informative.

“The four sets of questions represent the key components of psychopathy — manipulation, callousness, ­impulsivity and anti-sociality.

“An understanding of our less flattering tendencies can serve as a basis for self-improvement.

“As we spot areas to work on, we can challenge ourselves to behave more generously and helpfully than we might if left to our own devices.”

Poisonous People: Psychopathy, Narcissism, Manipulation, Sadism: How To Resist Them And Improve Your Life, by Leanne ten Brinke (Simon & Schuster, £22).



HOW YOU RELATE TO OTHERS

Have you ever:

Told a lie to get what you want.

Manipulated your family, friends or coworkers to your own advantage.

Pretended to like someone to get what you wanted.

Thought other people were “suckers” for believing your lies.

Felt cynical, believing that everyone is willing to screw you over to get what they want.

Wanted to be the centre of attention.

Felt like you’re special, and others are inferior.

Leanne says: “If you said yes to all or most of these, it’s a sign you could have selfish and manipulative traits.

“Rather than trying to connect with others, such people look at others as a means to an end.

“They may come across as charming, but that’s by design. They’ll say anything to get you to see them in a positive light or do what they want, lying far more than average.

“They have an inflated sense of self and need you to think highly of them.”



HOW YOU FEEL EMOTIONS

Have you ever:

Enjoyed watching someone else fail or experience pain.

Picked on someone just for the fun of it.

Been described as cold or callous.

Felt nothing when you saw someone else in pain.

Thought you were tougher than everyone else.

Enjoyed watching violent sporting events or movies.

Ignored a friend when they stopped being useful to you.

Thought that people respond far too emotionally at funerals, weddings or graduations.

Leanne says: “If you recall instances of all or most items in this section, it could be a sign of emotional deficits.

“People with psychopathic traits can simulate emotions, passing themselves off as warm, loving and affectionate – but in truth, they are cold, unfeeling and unempathetic.

“When they do wrong, they don’t experience remorse or accept responsibility, although they might sometimes act like they do if they perceive it to be in their interest.”

HOW YOU WEIGH UP RISK

Have you ever:



Sought out dangerous situations.

Responded aggressively to someone without thinking.

Considered yourself a “thrillseeker.”

Had sex with a stranger.

Enjoyed gambling for a significant sum of money.

Been easily bored.

Driven recklessly, just to feel alive.

Been described as reckless or irresponsible.

Leanne says: “This category has to do with a penchant for sensation-seeking and risk-taking. If you ticked off most of these items, it could be a sign that you are prone to boredom and constantly seek that next rush.

“Such people don’t think through their actions and behave irresponsibly. They’re addicted to the fast life – sex, drugs, gambling and power.

“Because they are such reckless, short-term thinkers, they tend to leach off others to get by.”

HOW YOU STICK TO RULES

Have you ever:

Shoplifted from a store.

Taken illegal drugs.

Got in a fist fight.

Been arrested or charged with a crime.

Got kicked out of a restaurant or other establishment for breaking their rules.

Broken into a car or building.

Tricked someone into giving you money.

Been suspended or expelled from school.

Leanne says: “If you said yes to most items in this section, it could be that you are prone to breaking rules, often in creative ways.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Some researchers argue that anti-social, often criminal behaviour, isn’t a defining quality of psychopathy, but rather a consequence of being ­manipulative, callous and impulsive. There might be something to that.

“If you have any one of these traits, you might end up behaving in ways that see you fall foul of the law.”

News.title: Criminal turned TikTok content creator reportedly detained in Vietnam
News.content:
Criminal turned TikTok content creator reportedly detained in Vietnam

Sam Walker has reportedly been detained in Vietnam, with a video allegedly showing him being arrested in the capital city of Hanoi

View Image Sam Walker during a video he posted as he appeared to be placed in a police vehicle in Vietnam

A Brit criminal-turned-TikTok content creator has reportedly been detained in Vietnam.

Sam Walker shared multiple videos of himself in the Southeast Asian nation in the days before his reported detention, as well as broadcasting live streams.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) is aware of Walker's alleged detention in the country, reports the Liverpool Echo. A family friend also confirmed to the Echo that he was detained on Saturday (April 4).

The FCDO is also believed to be liaising with local authorities following Walker's reported detention. It remains unclear why Walker, who has dozens of convictions for more than 130 offences, is said to have been detained in the country.

A video has subsequently been posted on Sam Walker's TikTok account that purportedly shows him being detained by Vietnamese police officers in the capital city of Hanoi. The footage shows Walker claiming to be followed by a police officer before cutting to him being approached and placed in the back of a police vehicle.

Walker previously appeared at Liverpool Crown Court in January this year, where a charge of sending a communication threatening serious harm was dropped. The court also heard that he had been "stabbed and shot", causing him to miss a previous court appearance, with him claiming to have been in A&E as a result of his injuries.

In 2024, it was reported Walker was detained in Sierra Leone after purportedly travelling to the West African nation in March of that year, stating he had fled the UK following bail after a separate arrest. His elaborate-sounding trip to Africa supposedly involved chartering a private aircraft and using a speedboat to traverse the Mediterranean to evade border controls after having his passport confiscated.

Walker maintains he went to Sierra Leone to assist children living in poverty. In a 2024 post on his TikTok and Instagram accounts, he said: "I'm going to the slums to get these kids their operations so they can see their families again."

However, his friend Samuel contacted the Echo to warn the public about Walker's alleged detention. Samuel said: "He's out in Sierra Leone and was doing a peaceful protest in the street.

Article continues below

"Then the police arrested him and put him in jail. That was four days ago. I'm really worried about him."

In a video shared at the time, Walker can be heard saying: "I will happily do prison. I don't give a s**t. You can put me in the most violent, filthy, unpredictable jail in the continent of Africa, and I promise you I will come out with my head held high."

The FCDO stated at the time: "We supported a British man in Sierra Leone and were in contact with the local authorities."

News.title: 'Eyesore' £10m mansion owned by Iran Government left to rot in UK for 16 years
News.content:
'Eyesore' £10m mansion owned by Iran Government left to rot in UK for 16 years

Brackendene mansion was built around 1900 and bought by Iran in the 1970s during the Shah's reign, but has been empty since 2010 and branded an 'eyesore' by locals

View 9 Images Brackendene mansion was built around 1900 and bought by Iran in the 1970s

This is the enormous mansion abandoned by the Iranian government in Cheshire's wealthy 'Golden Triangle' which has been labelled an 'eyesore' by residents as it deteriorates.

Haunting photographs have shown the dilapidated condition of the mock Tudor mansion which has been left to decay for the past 16 years but could fetch up to £10m. Brackendene in Trafford, Greater Manchester, was once a striking feature of the prosperous, leafy green neighbourhood.

The neglected red brick mansion overlooks the sweeping fields of the Cheshire Plains and is encircled by premium real estate worth millions. It was purchased by the Islamic Middle Eastern nation in the 1970s when pro-western monarch Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi ruled the country.

The mock-Tudor property is cloaked in mystery, but it's believed some of the grandest parties in the city would occur within the now decaying walls - and at one stage, even their consul-general resided there. Diplomatic and trade discussions as well as social gatherings and banquets are also thought to have occurred there.

View 9 Images The mansion has been left abandoned for 16 years

Yet now striking drone photographs reveal its pitiful condition left ransacked, with its once-manicured garden wild and untamed, and windows sealed with boards. Its greenhouse destroyed and outdoor pool covered with algae.

The dilapidated property - which was constructed around 1900 - has been officially unoccupied since 2010, according to Trafford Council. It's believed its decline began following the Islamic revolution in February 1979, says Amir Barik, a senior lecturer at Manchester Metropolitan University.

View 9 Images The mansion has fallen victim to vandalism and unsightly graffiti

The revolt resulted in Pahlavi being overthrown and replaced by what would become known as the Islamic Republic, led by Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, who was later declared the country's first Supreme Leader that December. Subsequent reports suggested the property deteriorated further after a 'collapse in relations' in 2005, when Iranian politicians urged the government to sever diplomatic ties with Britain.

Brackendene then fell victim to vandals who defaced it with unsightly graffiti and stripped it of any valuables - much to the dismay of local residents. Local inhabitant Deborah Jeffery said: "People pay a lot of money to live here because it is a quintessential English village.

View 9 Images It's believed its decline began following the Islamic revolution in February 1979

"I walk past it every day and have often thought what an amazing property and wondered what it would have looked like in its day. It is such a shame how it has been left, as the land around it is stunning.

"It's just waiting for someone to come along and snap it up and do it up really nice. I do wish they would come along sooner though, as it is an eyesore to the area."

View 9 Images Locals claimed the mansion was "an eyesore to the area"

Other nearby homeowners have also expressed similar desires to see it tidied up and restored to its former glory. In 2011, there appeared to be a breakthrough when it was reported that representatives from the Iranian embassy in London had journeyed to Trafford to discuss the building's future.

However, tensions surrounding Iran's nuclear programme escalated and turned violent. Furious protesters stormed the British embassy in Tehran, Iran's capital, after the Conservative–Liberal Democrat coalition government backed further sanctions. Subsequently, they gave Iranian diplomats 48 hours to exit the country.

View 9 Images There were three arson attacks within 11 months when it appeared there might be a resolution

During this period, three arson attacks within 11 months nearly destroyed the building - the final incident in 2011 was so severe it caused the upper floors to collapse into the basement. Despite this, council chiefs have taken steps to curb illegal activity with hopes of potentially reopening the building in the future.

The roof and several floors have been repaired following the fires by the Iranian owners, according to Trafford Council. A local estate agent estimates that the house and surrounding land, without planning permission, would be worth around £1.5million.

View 9 Images Nearby homeowners have expressed desires to see it tidied up and restored to its former glory

However, with the right planning and spec build, it could fetch around the £10million mark. Reclaiming the land is not straightforward for the council, as it sits on diplomatic land owned by the Iranian Government. That means the council cannot obtain a compulsory purchase order as they typically would for properties in similar situations.

‌



A compulsory purchase order (CPO) enables a public authority to acquire land without the owner's consent, according to national housing charity and campaign group Shelter. Trafford Council said it held numerous discussions with the Iranian Government following its closure about the 'state of the site' and its 'long-term use'. It also said it met with the owners on several occasions and 'stressed' their concerns while advising on 'additional measures to secure the site'.

View 9 Images The roof and several floors have been repaired following the fires by the Iranian owners

A spokesperson for Trafford Council said: "The former Consul-General's House and the surrounding land is owned by the Iranian Government and is governed by diplomatic procedures limiting the ability of the Council to intervene. In 2024, we wrote to a representative with regards to the repair of security fencing and on-site brick wall.

‌



"We also discussed the need to urgently find a long term use for Brackendene which is an important building and site in the Devisdale Conservation Area.

View 9 Images It's believed some of the grandest parties in the city would occur within the now decaying walls

"We noted that a number of rebuilding works appeared to have taken place on the site including re-roofing and new floors and we reminded the owners that building regulation approval was required from the Council.

Article continues below

"We have recommended to Iranian representatives that they should seek advice from a planning consultant and submit a pre-application enquiry to the Council so we can advise on any proposed developments they wish to make. We will continue to press the owners of the site to carry out works to make it safe and secure and to commit to a plan regarding the long-term use of the building."

News.title: Man, 20, charged with rape following Bristol city centre police probe
News.content:
Man, 20, charged with rape following Bristol city centre police probe

A 20-year-old man has been charged with rape and will appear at Bristol Magistrates' Court tomorrow

View Image The man will now appear at Bristol Magistrates Court (file) (Image: PA)

A 20-year-old man from Bristol has been charged in connection with an ongoing rape investigation.

‌



Nitesh Nitesh, of Byron Street in Redfield, faces one count of rape, and is due to appear at Bristol Magistrates' Court tomorrow (Monday). The charge comes following an investigation into the rape of a woman in the Assembly Rooms Lane area of Bristol at around 3.05am last Sunday, March 29.

‌



Two individuals have been released under investigation while enquiries remain ongoing. Avon and Somerset Police previously confirmed that officers first arrived at the scene within eight minutes of the rape being reported, and assisted in taking the victim to safety, reports Bristol Live.

‌



DI Simon Broad, from Avon and Somerset Police's Criminal Investigation Department (CID), said: "Our enquiries are ongoing and to date we have made three arrests in connection with this investigation."

"We continue to support and update the victim on our progress, and I would like to take this opportunity to praise her for the strength and courage she has demonstrated throughout.

Article continues below

"We would like to remind members of the public not to speculate online as this could impact our ongoing investigation and future judicial proceedings."

Anyone with information is urged to call 101, quoting reference number 5226085769, or fill in the online appeals form. You can also reach the independent charity Crimestoppers completely anonymously on 0800 555 111 or through their Anonymous Online Form.

No personal information is required, details cannot be traced or logged, and you will neither be called to court nor required to speak to police when getting in touch with Crimestoppers.

News.title: Night of carnage in Southend-on-Sea sees man 'hit by car and stabbed' as armed cops swoop
News.content:
Night of carnage in Southend-on-Sea sees man 'hit by car and stabbed' as armed cops swoop

A man has been left with potentially life-changing injuries and four people have been arrested following the events in Southend-on-Sea last night

View 2 Images Police were guarding a cordon this morning after the incident (Image: EssexLive)

Three men and a woman have been arrested following the events on Chichester Road in Southend-on-Sea last night

A man has been left with potentially life-changing injuries after being allegedly struck by a vehicle and stabbed in a night of carnage in Southend-on-Sea.

Police and paramedics rushed to Chichester Road in the Essex city in the early hours of Sunday (April 5) following reports of two groups brawling.

The unrest reportedly broke out at around 2am as the two groups of people, some thought to be carrying knives, started fighting in the seaside city, Essex Live reports.

Armed officers raced to the scene where a man with stab wounds was discovered. Further investigations indicate a vehicle had also been in collision with the man, who has suffered injuries described as serious and potentially life-changing, the force said.

View 2 Images A large cordon was erected on Chichester Road, at the junction with Warrior Square, into Sunday morning (Image: EssexLive)

Two suspects fled the scene in a vehicle, which was located at Southend Hospital. A second vehicle, also believed to have been involved in the incident, was safely stopped on the M25 in Hertfordshire.

Four people, three men and one woman, have been arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm. One of these, a man, remains in hospital for treatment. The incident is believed to be linked to an earlier disturbance which happened near South Street Bar in London Road, Westcliff, at around 1am, cops said.

A large cordon was erected on Chichester Road, at the junction with Warrior Square, into Sunday morning, with officers seen guarding the crime scene.

Chief Superintendent Chris Bradford said: “I understand how concerning this incident will be to the local community today. I want to reassure you that officers have made quick arrests and we believe that those involved are known to each other.

“You will see an increased policing presence in the area and I encourage you to come and talk to us. I would also ask anyone who has information, CCTV or dashcam footage to contact us. This investigation is in its early stages, but this type of violent behaviour has no place in Southend and we will not tolerate it."

A spokesperson for Essex Police added: "If you have any information, CCTV, dash cam or other footage in relation to this incident, then please get in contact with us. Please quote incident 42/51345/26.

Article continues below

"You can let us know by submitting a report on our website or by using our online Live Chat service which is available 24 hours-a-day, seven days-a-week. Visit www.essex.police.uk/digital101 to find out more about our online reporting services.

"If you would like to make an anonymous report you can contact independent charity Crimestoppers, by visiting their website or by calling 0800 555 111."

News.title: 'Evil' daughter stole £40k from sick mum and squandered it on clothes and takeaways
News.content:
'Evil' daughter stole £40k from sick mum and squandered it on clothes and takeaways

Michelle Moore admitted fraud at Chelmsford Crown Court after taking her mother Lynne Mill's money over three years while acting as her carer

View 7 Images Lynne had £40,000 stolen by her "evil" daughter

A vulnerable woman swindled out of £40,000 by her "evil" daughter says the ordeal almost left her homeless and has torn her family apart.

‌



Michelle Moore was given control of mum Lynne Mill's finances after her husband died and she was diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease in 2019. A court heard the 39-year-old had taken her 68-year-old mother's card under the guise of purchasing her groceries while providing care for her.

‌



But a court heard she instead squandered thousands of pounds on clothes and takeaways, leaving her destitute and facing eviction. Michelle's sister, Taryna Mills, says she was horrified when she eventually visited her mum's flat and found it in 'squalor'.

‌



Lynne was compelled to take her daughter to court to demonstrate to those pursuing her debts that she hadn't been managing her finances. The great-grandmother, who has 21 grandchildren, said she'd hoped a stint in prison would put her daughter back on track.

View 7 Images Taryna (L) and Lynne (R) said their family was torn apart after Michelle's swindling

‌



However, after Chelmsford Crown Court heard she was the sole carer of her five children, a judge suspended her prison sentence - telling her she should be 'thoroughly ashamed' of what she'd done. Lynne and Tarnya, 42, who has now assumed responsibility for her mother's care, say they were 'disgusted' that Michelle escaped a prison term.

"I couldn't believe she would do what she did," Lynne said. "She stole sweets from shops as a kid, like any child, but one time she came back with a bag full of makeup.

"I took her to Bexleyheath Police Station the next day and told them to lock her in a cell for an hour. I thought it would teach her a lesson, but obviously it didn't.

‌



"She said in court that she'd had a traumatic childhood, but she was the spoilt one. I knew what Michelle was like when she was younger, but I didn't think she would do anything like this.

"It has only been the court case that has made it all sink in. All I kept thinking was: I had five girls and I brought them all up the same... Why has she turned out like that?"

View 7 Images Lynne was left "living in squalor" under the care of Michelle

‌



Michelle started using her mother's card after becoming her carer in 2020, refusing to return it despite Lynne's repeated requests. She confessed to stealing more than £40,000 of her mother's money over three years - a sum which excludes weekly supermarket shops of up to £300, as these could not be proved as not being for Lynne.

Yet Lynne and Taryna claim the true amount taken exceeded £50,000, but that Michelle had agreed to plead guilty to charges concerning £40,000 to avoid going to trial. The court was told the money was transferred into bank accounts held by Michelle and her husband, Wayne.

Card transactions included payments to Amazon, Apple, Halfords, Primark, New Look, McDonald's, Just Eat and even sex toys and lingerie retailer Ann Summers.

‌



Tarnya says Michelle would reassure her that she was looking after their mother properly, while also impersonating her mother and requesting advance Universal Credit payments. "I've been caring for mum since Michelle left in August 2023," Tarnya explained.

7 View 7 Images Michelle used Lynne's money to fund her lifestyle 7 View 7 Images Michelle told Lynne she couldn't afford a cheap pair of slippers, before spending £700 in one night

‌



"The level of care was nothing like what my sister was making out. We were all brought up in the same household - all five of us under one roof. She was the youngest and, out of all of us, she had it best."

Things reached breaking point in August 2023 when, during the height of summer, Mrs Mills asked her daughter to purchase a £40 fan - only to be told by Moore she couldn't afford it. A row followed, with Michelle throwing her mother's card back at her and ringing her sister to announce she would no longer be providing care.

When Tarnya stepped into her mum's flat, she was stunned by its condition. She discovered that, alongside empty cupboards, there weren't even any sheets on her mum's bed.

‌



"It was in squalor," mum-of-four Tarnya said. "I was shocked. I hadn't been in there, because of Covid and because I was caring for mum's mum. We were in different bubbles. Obviously, you feel guilt, but you just don't expect a family member to do what she did."

Tarnya revealed her mum had also been requesting Michelle to send money to her grandchildren for birthdays and Christmas. "They never received a penny," she said. "It was all going into Michelle's pocket.

"You don't expect it from a carer, but you certainly don't expect it from your own daughter. For dinner, mum would get a bit of cold pizza brought round, or some Chinese or the leftovers of whatever Michelle's family had eaten the night before.

‌



View 7 Images Michelle was spared jail

"I asked her for a couple of pairs of slippers from Primark once," Lynne added. "They were a pound each. Michelle told me I didn't have enough money. That same day, she went into Colchester and spent about £700.

"Michelle's daughter would say to me, 'Mummy used your card in Morrison's. I will nick it back off her and give it back to you'. That was from a nine-year-old. Even her children knew it was wrong."

‌



Having changed her plea to guilty on the day of her trial, Michelle's sentencing was delayed on multiple occasions while social services reports were compiled on each of her children. When the day finally came, Lynne revealed she had been eagerly anticipating her daughter receiving the justice she deserved.

"I was looking forward to the court date," she said. "Michelle was going to get her just desserts. If she was locked up, even just for one day and night, it might be enough. She would see what it's like.

"But it didn't work out like that... Now, she's laughing. She's a greedy woman. She cares for no one but herself."

‌



Tarnya also revealed she had heard that Michelle had been spotted laughing while getting a tattoo in Clacton the day after her sentencing. She reckons her sister deliberately waited until their mother's death was imminent before changing her plea, believing she could escape justice without her mum alive to challenge her version of events.

"It's all the lies," Tarnya said. "If you've done something, own up to it. Don't use your children to get out of it, which is what she did. I wanted her to realise what she had done to our mum was wrong, but even the judge said she hadn't shown any remorse.

View 7 Images Taryna has since cleared her mum's "astronomical debt"

‌



"Now she could do this again, to an elderly neighbour or something. If you can do it to your own mum, you can do it to anyone. You shouldn't do what Michelle did to anyone, but to do it to your own mother?

"That makes you the lowest of the low - and she hasn't even been punished for it. Michelle is evil, disgusting... lower than low. The rest of us have stuck together, but no one wants anything to do with her. Mum has lost her grandchildren as well. It has broken the family apart."

Tarnya says she's now cleared all her mum's 'astronomical' debts, with the family currently planning to redecorate her flat in Clacton. Yet despite attempting to move forward, Lynne says she can never erase what one of her own daughters did to destroy her life.

Article continues below

"I will never forgive Michelle for what she's done," Lynne said. "I don't even want her to know when I die. I don't want her at my funeral."

Judge Jamie Sawyer handed Michelle Moore a two-year suspended prison sentence after she admitted a single count of fraud by false representation on the day of her trial in September last year. He also ordered her to carry out 150 hours of community service and pay £1,000 in compensation to her mother, while acknowledging that this was a 'drop in the ocean' compared to what she had taken. Michelle was additionally issued with a restraining order, barring her from making any contact with her mother Lynne or sister Tarnya.

News.title: Nottingham grocery store owner 'masterminded £40m cigarette smuggling network'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Nottingham grocery store owner 'masterminded £40m cigarette smuggling network'

Hasan Ferhat Baybasin has been arrested as part of an international anti-mafia investigation into a vast network of tobacco smugglers moving huge illegal shipments around the world

View 7 Images Hasan Ferhat Baybasin appeared in court last week (Image: Europol)

The owner of a Nottingham grocery store has been arrested on suspicion of masterminding a £40million international cigarette smuggling network.

Hasan Ferhat Baybasin, 34, was held as part of a huge operation spanning five countries led by the Anti-Mafia Investigative Directorate (DIA) in Italy. Officers seized over 40 tonnes of illegal cigarettes worth around £40m along with assets worth over £2million.

Baybasin, from Edgware, north London, appeared at Westminster Magistrates' court on Thursday alongside codefendant Cagdas Duran, 37. The defendants, who are both directors of the Target Food Store on Alfreton Road in Radford, Nottingham, were remanded in custody to face extradition proceedings.

View 7 Images Hasan Ferhat Baybasin (left) and Cagdas Duran (Image: Europol)

A judge in Genoa, Italy, ordered the pre-trial detention of the pair along with three other alleged gang members held in Italy and Poland. According to the European Public Prosecutor's Office, the cigarette smugglers used a number of complex maritime routes to evade customs.

View 7 Images Their shop in Nottingham (Image: Google Maps)

The cargo originated in Armenia, going through Dubai and on to Spain before entering Italy at the port of Genoa. Other routes passed through Georgia, Kenya, the Netherlands and Turkey, as the gang attempted to conceal the true origin of the illegal goods.

The organisation had established a network of accomplices across the world, and the cigarettes were destined for the black market in the UK and other European nations.

View 7 Images Italian law enforcement seize the illegal cargo (Image: Europol)

They allegedly claimed they were shipping building materials and used containers with false bottoms to hide their illegal cargo. A corrupt IT specialist is said to have created and managed fake websites and emails as a front for the network while the plotters used sophisticated encrypted phones to avoid law enforcement.

The market value of the seized goods in Italy is estimated at around £15million, a figure that could have tripled had they reached the UK. Baybasin is understood to be a member of a notorious family that founded the Hackney Bombers organised crime gang in north east London.

Huseyin Baybasin, 68, became known as “Europe’s Pablo Escobar” when he masterminded the export of vast quantities of heroin while leading the network in the 1990s. The group has been locked in a bloody war with the rival Tottenham Turks gang that has seen at least a dozen murders.

View 7 Images Officers search the boxes of illegal tobacco (Image: Handout)

A leading figure of the Bombers was the intended target of a shooting at a restaurant in Dalston, North East London, in May 2024 that left a nine-year-old girl with a bullet lodged in her head.

Six weeks later, senior Tottenham Turks member Izzet Eren, 41, was shot and killed outside a cafe in Chisinau, Moldova, in what is believed to be a tit-for-tat attack.

View 7 Images The gunman on a motorbike who shot the little girl (Image: PA)

The Bombers, or Bombacilar as they are known in Turkish, acquired a fearsome reputation when it was run by Huseyin Baybasin and two brothers, known as “The Family".

Huseyin was arrested in Holland while his brother Abdullah, 64, who was confined to a wheelchair after being shot by a rival in the 1980s, arrived in Britain via Gibraltar in 1997.

Third brother Mehmet, 60, worked with Liverpool gangs to import vast quantities of cocaine into the UK from Latin America. Mehmet, who lived in Edgware, Middlesex, travelled to South America regularly for meetings with representatives of Colombian and Venezuelan cartels.

View 7 Images Izzet Eren (top right) along with fellow gang members (Image: PA)

He is currently serving a 30-year sentence in Whitemoor prison, Cambs, for attempting to import 40 tonnes of cocaine after he was jailed in Liverpool in 2011.

Article continues below

Huseyin, a Kurd, has been in custody in Holland since 1998, and has now been cleared to work on his return to society by the Advisory Board for Long-Term Sentences.

Abdullah's son Cagdas Baybasin was repeatedly shot in Düsseldorf, Germany in January. Abdullah was jailed in London for 22 years in 2006 for supplying heroin and later deported.

News.title: New anti-terror attack advice unveiled in Manchester Arena victim's memory
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: New anti-terror attack advice unveiled in Manchester Arena victim's memory

Home Office chiefs will publish advice on how venues can implement Martyn’s Law - passed in memory of Manchester Arena victim Martyn Hett

View 4 Images Martyn, 29, was one of 22 killed in the Manchester Arena bombing (Image: PA)

Crucial anti-terror guidance aimed at preventing another atrocity like the 2017 Manchester Arena bombing is to be released within weeks.

‌



Home Office chiefs will publish advice on how tens of thousands of venues, from music arenas and football stadiums to schools and community centres, can implement Martyn’s Law. The landmark legislation is named in memory of Manchester Arena victim Martyn Hett, 29, who was one of 22 killed by a suicide bomber after an Ariana Grande concert.

‌



Martyn’s Law will require venues with a capacity of more than 200 to have plans in place to prevent terror attacks. Those that can accommodate over 800 will be required to use advanced CCTV or hire more security staff.

‌



View 4 Images Figen Murray has tirelessly campaigned to make venues safer (Image: PA)

The government guidance is being released ahead of the legislation coming into force next year following a two-year consultation period. Some venues, including Manchester Arena, now known as the AO Arena, have already implemented safety measures, such as a screening system that forensically scans crowds for terror threats.

London’s Madame Tussauds and Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, plus Manchester’s Lowry Theatre and Bridgwater Hall, have also invested in anti-terror technology. Some schools, colleges and universities are taking early action by practising lockdowns and other safety measures.

‌



View 4 Images New government guidance is set to be released soon (Image: PA)

Coronation Street superfan Martyn, a PR manager, was on a farewell night out with pals before heading to the US when terrorist Salman Abedi, 22, detonated a bomb packed with nuts and bolts, killing 22 concertgoers and injuring more than 1,000 others.

His mum Figen Murray, who has campaigned for tighter security ever since, said: “The new guidance will be pivotal and will allow venues the chance to make the whole nation safer. It will make us the world leader in anti-terror security.

Article continues below

View 4 Images Martyn's Law received Royal Assent on April 3, 2025 (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"Hopefully this time next year I can sit back and know I have done my duty to the nation and Martyn, and happily say our venues are the safest in the world.”

Some rogue operators have been attempting to cash in on Martyn’s Law by scaremongering businesses into paying to make themselves compliant, without any government guidance having yet been issued. Figen said she hoped that the new Home Office guidance, which is expected this month, a year after the bill received royal assent, will stop these firms and give venues a clear roadmap.

News.title: 'Trump's expletive-laden rant threatening to bomb Iran is chaos dressed up as toughness'
News.content:
'Trump's expletive-laden rant threatening to bomb Iran is chaos dressed up as toughness'

"At a moment of rising tension, the world needs calm heads and careful judgment. Instead, it gets bluster, bravado and instability with real-world consequences"

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

A president’s words should steady a crisis, not inflame it. Donald Trump has done the opposite.

‌



His foul-mouthed rant threatening to bomb Iran, dressed up as “Power Plant Day”, was not just crude - it was deeply alarming. Laced with expletives and a sneering, tone-deaf slight at Islam, it read less like leadership and more like a man losing control at the very moment calm is needed most.

‌



One minute, Trump talks of striking a deal. Next, he threatens to “blow everything up”. That is not strategy, it is chaos dressed up as toughness.

‌



At a moment of rising tension, the world needs calm heads and careful judgment. Instead, it gets bluster, bravado and instability with real-world consequences.

America and its allies need grown-ups in the room. Because right now, the man in charge looks less like a statesman and more like a man-child playing with fire.

Royal Family's newest members join William and Kate for debut at Easter service READ MORE :

'Reform council goes disastrously wrong'

‌



Kent County Council should ring alarm bells across Britain - a blueprint for how disastrously wrong things can go when voters buy the hype and ignore the warning signs. Reform UK promised a “new dawn”.

What Kent has got instead is chaos, infighting and precious little improvement in people’s daily lives. Residents see no real change.

Roads aren’t maintained, services are stretched, and charities say demand is as high as ever. Inside County Hall, it’s even worse - rows, resignations and a toxic atmosphere where point-scoring trumps progress.

‌



If this is Reform’s “shop window”, it is like Carry on Council without the jokes. Local government should deliver, not perform. Ahead of next month’s polls, voters should look hard at Kent, because this is exactly what happens when slogans give way to substance.

'Royal reminder of strength and resilience'

A welcome sight at Windsor: unity, warmth and renewal. The Prince and Princess of Wales returning with their children after a difficult year was a powerful reminder of strength and resilience.

Article continues below

Alongside the King and Queen, it showed a Royal Family focused on duty and togetherness - all the stronger for the absence of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Sarah Ferguson.

A fresh chapter, and all the better for it.

News.title: 'Unbelievable!': Backshall overjoyed at rare sighting of orcas
News.content:
Wildlife explorer Steve Backshall was overjoyed to have spotted two of the UK's last surviving orcas as he described them as "international celebrities".

Male killer whales John Coe and Aquarius are the last remaining members of the West Coast Community pod.

The bulls were seen off Lizard Point on Wednesday and filmed by the TV presenter, who lives near Penzance, in Cornwall.

The brothers had last been seen off the west coast of Cornwall in May 2021.

Fans of two cherished California bald eagles were glued to a livestream as both of their chicks hatched from their eggs this Easter weekend.

Two hatchlings belonging to Jackie and Shadow — a pair of beloved bald eagles living in Big Bear Lake just outside Los Angeles — were born this weekend.

The first chick arrived around 9:30 p.m. PST on Saturday, while the second hatched around 8:30 a.m. PST Easter morning, according to the nonprofit Friends of Big Bear Valley.

Jackie and Shadow have a devoted fanbase, thanks to two 24-hour cameras operated by the nonprofit that allow fans to watch the birds from their nest.

Little chirps were heard from the eggs on Thursday, before the first of the two chicks slowly pushed its way through the hard membrane of its egg and was welcomed into the world by their parents.

open image in gallery Popular California bald eagles Jackie and Shadow saw two eaglets hatch leading in time for Easter ( Friends of Big Bear Valley and Big Bear Eagle Nest Cam/Facebook )

Eaglets are not considered hatched until they are completely free of their egg shell, the nonprofit said. It can take anywhere from 24 to 48 hours for a chick to fully hatch after breaking their shell.

“The chick has popped its head out of the shell to say a happy hatch day to mom and dad!” the nonprofit wrote on Saturday, as the first chick began to hatch.

At that time, it appeared that the second egg had a pip, or a hole pecked in the shell by the chick.

The second hatchling didn’t make their way out of their egg until Sunday morning, just in time for Easter.

“Shadow arrived a bit after the 2nd hatch and saw his two tiny eaglets for the first time,” the nonprofit said in a Facebook post on Sunday. “

“He seemed quite proud and didn’t waste any time snuggling in for daddy duty. Both chicks are doing well, looking great and their journey has just begun,” the group added.

Footage from the livestream showed one of the eagle parents covering its babies for warmth just after 9 a.m. Sunday, after the two had both fully hatched.

Jackie and Shadow have been in the spotlight for years ever since Friends of Big Bear Valley set up a nest camera to provide around-the-clock coverage of the two beloved birds.

The feathered parents have parented eaglets in 2019, 2022 and 2025, raising chicks Simba and Cookie (2019), Spirit (2022) and Sunny and Gizmo (2025).

open image in gallery The babies can take anywhere from 24 to 48 hours to fully exit their eggs ( Friends of Big Bear Valley and Big Bear Eagle Nest Cam/Facebook )

The nonprofit holds an annual fundraising naming contest to decide the names of the chicks.

Local third-grade students get the final vote on what the baby birds will be named.

“Congratulations Jackie and Shadow on your first hatch of the season,” the nonprofit wrote on its website.

While it was once considered a threatened and endangered species, the bald eagle was removed from the list in 2007, according to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.

However, the bald eagle is still considered an endangered species under the California Endangered Species Act, which classifies it as a “fully protected” bird in the state.

Bald eagles are protected nationwide under the Migratory Bird Treaty Act and the Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act, which bans the killing, selling or otherwise harming of eagles, their nests or eggs.

The Friends of Big Bear Valley Eagle Cam livestreams can be viewed on the group’s website.

Storm Dave caused travel chaos and left homes without power as it swept across northern parts of the UK, bringing heavy snow and strong winds.

Gusts reached 93mph at Capel Curig in North Wales, while winds of 75mph were recorded at Emley Moor in West Yorkshire and St Bees Head in Cumbria, and one of 73mph was recorded at Buchan in Aberdeenshire, the Met Office said.

Some properties in Scotland were left without power following the high winds overnight. Scottish and Southern Electricity Networks (SSEN) fault response teams were out on the network working to reconnect the small number of customers affected, mainly in Skye, Caithness and coastal parts of Aberdeenshire.

There was snow in Skye and other parts of western Scotland, including Inverclyde, while Glasgow saw snow late in the morning on Easter Sunday and there were snow flurries elsewhere in central Scotland.

Some Caledonian MacBrayne ferry services on Scotland’s west coast were disrupted by the weather, and some motorists faced disruption due to fallen trees blocking routes. Several major bridges in Scotland also had restrictions due to the high winds, including the Queensferry Crossing and the Forth Road Bridge near Edinburgh.

Speed limits were put in place causing delays for ScotRail passengers, while Network Rail replaced trains between Manchester Piccadilly and Chester with buses.

In Dublin, pilots faced challenging conditions as they attempted to land in the blustery weather. The airport cancelled 17 flights, causing further travel disruption into the Bank Holiday weekend as crews were displaced.

open image in gallery The amber weather warning was in place until 3am on Sunday ( PA Wire )

The amber weather warning was in place until 3am on Sunday and the Met Office warned of "severe gales" with flying debris and large waves, which could result in injuries and danger to life.

Three yellow warnings across parts of northern England, Scotland and Wales had been due to remain in place until midday on Easter Sunday but were lifted by around 7.30am as the weather improved.

Met Office spokesperson Marco Petagna said: “The winds eased down a bit more quickly than forecast across Scotland, northern England and Wales.

“Storm Dave is pulling away and the warnings are easing more quickly than forecast so the yellow warnings were no longer warranted.”

There are now no weather warnings in place for this week so far.

open image in gallery The weather warnings for storm Dave have now lifted ( Met Office )

The Met Office’s forecast for Easter Sunday said: “Storm Dave will clear north east on Sunday morning, leaving sunshine and widespread showers across the UK.

“Northern areas will see the heaviest blustery showers and feel cold, while temperatures elsewhere stay closer to average for early April.”

As of 9pm on Sunday, there was one flood warning and 16 flood alerts in place in England, while those in Scotland and Wales had lifted.

Weekend weather forecast

Sunday:

Cloud, rain and hill snow across the far North East clearing, as winds continue to ease. Sunny spells and blustery showers for many, but southern areas may to stay dry. Chilly.

Monday:

Winds will ease as Storm Dave clears into the North Sea on Sunday. Blustery showers will continue across Scotland and Northern Ireland while much of England and Wales will become fine.

Easter Monday will be the driest day of the Easter weekend, with a ridge of high pressure in the wake of Storm Dave bringing a more settled day. Most areas will see some sunny spells after a chilly night.

Zendaya’s newest movie has ended her eight-year streak of dominating the box office during opening weekend.

The Drama, starring the 29-year-old Euphoria star alongside Robert Pattinson, debuted at the third spot in the domestic chart over Easter weekend, marking the first Zendaya movie to not jump to the top spot upon release since her animated movie Smallfoot in 2018.

All six of Zendaya’s feature films released between Smallfoot’s premiere and The Drama — Spider-Man: Far From Home (2019), Space Jam: A New Legacy (2021), Dune: Part One (2021), Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021), Dune: Part Two (2024) and Challengers (2024) — debuted at number one during their respective opening weekends.

Kristoffer Borgli’s dark comedy did well for an A24 movie and made out with $14.4 million, which surpasses the studio’s 2025 rom-com Materialists. However, it was not enough to beat out Ryan Gosling’s space epic Project Hail Mary, which landed in second place during its third weekend behind the opening for the record-breaking The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.

The animated sequel recorded the biggest opening day of the year at the box office Friday with $48.3 million domestically and is set to become the highest-grossing Hollywood film of 2026 so far.

open image in gallery Robert Pattinson and Zendaya star in ‘The Drama’ by director Kristoffer Borgli ( A24 )

open image in gallery ‘Super Mario Galaxy Movie’ landed the top box office spot during its opening weekend ( AP )

After Project Hail Mary brought in a domestic opening weekend of $80.5 million last month, making the biggest of the year at that point, the movie was surpassed when the Super Mario Galaxy Movie soared to a massive $130.9 million in the three-day holiday weekend.

The first Mario Bros. Movie hit theaters over the same Easter weekend in 2023 and boasted a three-day weekend win of $147 million, one of the best showing of all time for a holiday.

Although The Drama did not catch up to its competitors in ticket sales, the dark comedy has become a popular topic of discourse surrounding its release due to a controversial plot twist that saw it condemned by critics before it even hit theaters.

open image in gallery Zendaya stars in 'The Drama,' which opened on Easter weekend with a $14 million domestic box office haul ( Getty Images )

The movie, which is produced by Hereditary’s Ari Aster, stars Zendaya and Pattinson as an engaged couple who question their relationship after Zendaya’s character Emma reveals a dark secret. The film also stars Alana Haim, Mamoudou Athie, Hailey Benton Gates and Zoë Winters.

Zendaya will have a chance to restart her hot streak with her next film appearances on the docket — two of which also coincidentally star Pattinson.

Her next movie to hit theaters will be Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey in July before Spider-Man: Brand New Day releases two weeks later. Then in December, she’ll join Pattinson and Timothée Chalamet in Dune: Part Three.

A long-serving Waitrose employee has spoken of feeling "demoralised" and "frustrated" after being dismissed for confronting a shoplifter attempting to steal Easter eggs.

Walker Smith, 54, a 17-year employee at the Clapham Junction branch, described Waitrose as "like my family". He claims his dismissal followed an attempt to stop a shoplifter with a bag full of Lindt Gold Bunny Easter eggs.

Mr Smith grabbed the bag, leading to a brief struggle before it snapped and its contents fell. The shoplifter fled, and Mr Smith, "out of frustration", threw a piece of a broken chocolate bunny towards some shopping trollies.

open image in gallery ( Getty Images )

"When I got home, I was punching myself and thinking: ‘Why did I do that?’" Mr Smith told The Guardian, having been dismissed two days later in a meeting with store managers. Waitrose stated current reports do not present the "full facts of the situation", emphasising that "nothing we sell is worth risking lives for".

Recalling his dismissal, Mr Smith said: "I tried to stay strong and I didn’t say a word, but inside I was crying. They led me out the back door by the bins. I just felt demoralised."

He added: "Waitrose is like my family. My friends are there. I was there for 17 years, I must have been doing something right. I’m not a bad or violent or aggressive person. I just got frustrated seeing this day in and day out and not seeing Waitrose do much about it."

Mr Smith, diagnosed with anxiety, claims managers were aware. Despite regretting his actions, he told The Guardian he was driven to intervene after witnessing thefts "every hour of every day for the last five years" without permission.

open image in gallery Waitrose stated current reports do not present the ‘full facts of the situation’, emphasising that ‘nothing we sell is worth risking lives for’

The incident comes amid a rise in shoplifting offences across England and Wales.

ONS figures show 519,381 offences to September 2025, a 5% increase from the previous year, slightly below the record 530,439 offences recorded to March 2025.

The Conservatives recently reiterated their commitment to "Good Samaritan" protections for retail staff. Shadow Justice Minister Kieran Mullan said "punishing people who step in to stop crime is wrong" and that people doing the "right thing" were being penalised.

Waitrose told the Press Association that the "safety and security" of its workers and customers underpins policies against staff intervening in thefts, explaining: "We’ve had incidents where our Partners have been hospitalised when challenging shoplifters. Luckily, they have always recovered, but that might not always be the case. There is a serious danger to life in tackling shoplifters. We refuse to put anyone’s life at risk and that’s why we have policies in place that are very clearly understood and must be strictly followed. As a responsible employer, we never want to be in a position where we are notifying families of a tragedy because someone tried to stop a theft. Nothing we sell is worth risking lives for. The reporting on this does not cover the full facts of the situation."

While not discussing Mr Smith’s case, Waitrose confirmed the "correct process" was followed, including an appeals procedure.
